items.title: How do Supervised Learning and Unsupervised Learning differ from each other?
items.content: Supervised learning involves training on labeled datasets to predict specific outputs, whereas unsupervised learning discovers patterns in unlabeled data or groups similar inputs together.

items.title: What is Reinforcement Learning and how does it relate to ANNs?
items.content: Reinforcement learning involves training through interactions with an environment, receiving rewards or penalties for actions taken. ANNs learn by trial and error, adapting to the environment's feedback.

items.title: What are some common types of activation functions in ANNs?
items.content: Common activation functions include ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit), Sigmoid, and Tanh. These introduce non-linearity into ANN inputs, enabling them to learn complex relationships.

items.title: What is the purpose of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)?
items.content: CNNs are designed for image and video analysis, using convolutional and pooling layers to extract features from data.

items.title: Can Transfer Learning be applied to any type of machine learning task?
items.content: No, transfer learning typically applies to tasks with similar datasets or feature structures, such as image classification or natural language processing.
